old: it was even greater than Elizabeth's
new: it still fell short of Elizabeth's
source: on the part of Mrs. Bennet and Kitty, though she was perfectly unknown to them, even inferior to what Elizabeth felt
reason: Source says Mrs. Bennet's and Kitty's astonishment was even inferior to (less than) Elizabeth's; the candidate inverts the comparison.

old: May I ask whether you left
new: May I take the liberty of asking your Ladyship whether you left
source: May I take the liberty of asking your Ladyship whether you left Mr. and Mrs. Collins well?
reason: Drops Mrs. Bennet's deferential formula and the form of address 'your Ladyship', flattening her awed obsequiousness toward rank.

new: extraordinary sources of happiness
source: such extraordinary sources of happiness necessarily attached to her situation
reason: 'Advantages' makes Elizabeth's reply sound mercenary; source says 'sources of happiness', keeping her ironic ambiguity.

new: all the more pitiable
source: That will make your Ladyship's situation at present more pitiable
reason: Elizabeth's barb is that Lady Catherine will be pitiable; 'unpleasant' blunts the insult.

new: But what was your mother?
source: But what was your mother?
reason: 'What' asks about her mother's social station (an attorney's daughter); 'who' loses the class sneer.

new: She insisted on going.
source: she would go
reason: 'She would go' means she insisted on leaving; 'had to go' implies an external obligation.

new: they obligingly satisfied their curiosity
source: they obligingly satisfied it with the same kind of supposition
reason: Narrator's ironic 'obligingly' (the family conveniently explains it away themselves) is dropped.

new: and wide powers of patronage
source: splendid property, noble kindred, and extensive patronage
reason: Patronage (the power to bestow livings and posts) is exactly what Collins, a clergyman owing his living to a patron, values; 'connections' changes the meaning.

old: I almost prefer him to Wickham
new: I can't help preferring him even to Wickham
source: I cannot help giving him the preference even over Wickham
reason: Candidate adds a hedge ('almost'); Mr. Bennet says he does prefer Collins even to Wickham.

old: Instead of receiving the expected excuses from his friend,
new: Instead of receiving the letter of excuse from his friend that Elizabeth half expected,
source: Instead of receiving any such letter of excuse from his friend, as Elizabeth half expected Mr. Bingley to do
reason: Loses that the expectation was Elizabeth's, and only a half-expectation; 'the expected excuses' makes it general and certain.

new: behaved beyond reproach
source: The conduct of neither, if strictly examined, will be irreproachable
reason: Elizabeth's understatement (not irreproachable) is inflated into flatly 'did not behave well'.

old: has been, and remains, unbearably painful
new: is now, and has been for many months, unbearably painful
source: is now, and has been many months, inexpressibly painful to me
reason: Drops 'many months', the duration of Darcy's remorse.

new: from ignorance
source: not of philosophy, but, what is much better, of ignorance
reason: Darcy's teasing paradox is 'ignorance' (of anything to reproach herself with); 'innocence' is a softened interpretation that removes the joke.

old: But we had considered it impossible—we had even discussed it.
new: But we had considered it—had talked of it—as impossible.
source: But we considered it, we talked of it as impossible.
reason: 'We had even discussed it' suggests they discussed it as a possibility; source says they talked of it as impossible.

old: Elizabeth reserved her mother's reaction for herself.
new: Elizabeth reserved for herself the task of asking her mother's.
source: Elizabeth reserved to herself the application for her mother's
reason: Source means Elizabeth kept to herself the job of asking her mother's consent; 'reserved her mother's reaction' is garbled.

new: equally unlikely to do credit to her good sense
source: her manner would be equally ill adapted to do credit to her sense
reason: Drops what the manner would be unsuitable for: showing Mrs. Bennet's sense.

new: anything he condescended to ask
source: to whom I should never dare refuse anything, which he condescended to ask
reason: Drops 'condescended', Mr. Bennet's dry irony about Darcy's hauteur.

new: think better of it
source: But let me advise you to think better of it.
reason: 'Think better of it' urges her to change her mind; 'think carefully' softens the advice.

new: drawn away from the pursuit of accomplishments
source: she was necessarily drawn from the pursuit of accomplishments
reason: Mary's accomplishments include music as well as reading; 'her books' narrows the source.

new: to make his fortune for him
source: Darcy might yet be prevailed on to make his fortune
reason: Source is about Darcy making Wickham rich (as Lydia's begging letter shows), not merely career advancement.

new: from a sister more than ten years younger than himself
source: which a brother will not always allow in a sister more than ten years younger than himself
reason: Drops the specific age gap.
